lesson.title: Finding an Item and Checking Out at a Supermarket

concept.explanation_zh: 当你在商店里找不到想要的东西时，如何礼貌且有效地向店员求助。这包括适当的表达方式和用词，帮助你顺利找到商品。
examples: Excuse me, could you help me find the cereal aisle?
Hi, do you know where the baking supplies are?
Sorry to bother you, but I'm looking for gluten-free bread.
concept.common_mistake_zh: 常见错误是直接说“Where is …?”，显得不够礼貌。正确的表达应该加上礼貌用语，比如“Could you please tell me where … is?”。

vocabulary.pronunciation_tip_zh: 注意双元音 /aɪ/，像汉语“艾”的音，末尾轻轻发 /l/ 音。
vocabulary.explain_in_english: An aisle is a passage between shelves in a store.
vocabulary.usage_note_zh: 常用在购物或超市场景，正式或非正式都适用。
examples: The cereal aisle is on the left side of the store.
I walked down the aisle looking for the cleaning products.

vocabulary.pronunciation_tip_zh: 注意连读，'checkout'中/t/和/ʃ/紧接，'counter'重音在第一个音节。
vocabulary.explain_in_english: The place in a store where you pay for your items.
vocabulary.usage_note_zh: 购物时必到的地方，正式非正式均可。
examples: I waited in line at the checkout counter.
She forgot her wallet at the checkout counter.

vocabulary.pronunciation_tip_zh: 'price'中的 /praɪs/ 注意双元音 /aɪ/，'tag'的 /æ/ 发音像汉语“啊”的音。
vocabulary.explain_in_english: A small label showing the price of a product.
vocabulary.usage_note_zh: 购物时查看商品价格常用词汇，适合所有正式和非正式场合。
examples: Check the price tag before you put it in your cart.
The price tag says $5, but the cashier charged me $7.

scene.title: Finding Gluten-Free Items and Checking Out
scene.context_zh: 在超市寻找无麸质食品并结账的自然对话。
scene.script_en:
Customer: Excuse me, could you help me find the gluten-free bread?
Store Clerk: Sure! It’s in aisle 5, next to the organic products.
Customer: Thanks! Also, do you know if the price tag there is accurate? Sometimes prices on shelves are different.
Store Clerk: Good question. Usually, the price tags are correct, but if you want, I can double-check at the checkout counter for you.
Customer: That would be great, thanks. By the way, do you accept credit cards here?
Store Clerk: Yes, we do. You can pay at any checkout counter.
Customer: Perfect. I’ll grab a few items and head over.
(After shopping)
Customer: Hi, I’m ready to check out.
Cashier: Hello! Did you find everything you needed?
Customer: Yes, thank you. Can you confirm the price of this bread?
Cashier: Let me scan it for you. It’s $4.99.
Customer: Great, thanks. Here’s my card.
Cashier: Thank you. Your total is $24.50. Have a nice day!
Customer: You too! Thanks for your help.
scene.translation_zh:
顾客：打扰一下，您能帮我找到无麸质面包吗？
店员：当然！在5号过道，靠近有机产品那边。
顾客：谢谢！另外，您知道那里的价格标签准确吗？有时候货架上的价格不同。
店员：好问题。通常价格标签是正确的，但如果您愿意，我可以帮您在结账柜台再确认一下。
顾客：那太好了，谢谢。顺便问一下，这里接受信用卡吗？
店员：是的，我们接受。您可以在任何结账柜台付款。
顾客：太好了。我拿几样东西就去结账。
（购物后）
顾客：您好，我准备结账了。
收银员：您好！您找到需要的东西了吗？
顾客：找到了，谢谢。您能确认一下这面包的价格吗？
收银员：让我给您扫描一下。是4.99美元。
顾客：太好了，谢谢。这是我的卡。
收银员：谢谢。您的总共是24.50美元。祝您有美好的一天！
顾客：您也是！谢谢您的帮助。
scene.practice_tip_zh: 练习时，尝试将对话中的礼貌用语如'excuse me'和'could you help me'熟记并自然使用，这样在真实购物时你会更有信心开口求助。

reading.title: A Letter to My Friend About a Supermarket Experience
reading.text_en:
Hi Alex,

I hope you’re doing well! I wanted to tell you about my last visit to GreenMart, the new supermarket that opened near my apartment. I was looking for some gluten-free items because my doctor recommended I try to avoid gluten. At first, I couldn’t find the gluten-free bread, and the price tags on some shelves were a bit confusing. I wasn’t sure if the prices were correct.

So, I asked a store clerk for help. She was very friendly and quickly showed me where the gluten-free section was. She also explained that sometimes prices on shelves don’t match the checkout prices, so it’s a good idea to ask if you want to be sure. That was helpful because I didn’t want any surprises when paying.

When I finished shopping, I went to the checkout counter. The cashier greeted me warmly and even double-checked the price of the bread for me. Paying by credit card was easy, and the total was exactly what I expected.

Overall, it was a positive experience. I’m glad I asked for help instead of wandering around confused. It reminded me that being polite and clear when you ask questions really makes a difference. Next time you visit, I think you’ll find the store easy to navigate, especially if you ask the staff for help.

Hope to catch up soon!

Best,
[Your Name]
reading.summary_zh: 这是一封写给朋友的非正式信，讲述作者在新开的超市购物时，如何寻找无麸质食品、询问价格标签和结账的经历。作者强调了礼貌求助的重要性，并鼓励朋友下次也试试。

questions.question: Why did the writer ask a store clerk for help?
questions.answer: Because they couldn’t find the gluten-free bread and were unsure about the accuracy of the price tags.

questions.question: What advice did the store clerk give about the price tags?
questions.answer: The clerk said that sometimes the prices on shelves don’t match the checkout prices, so it’s good to ask to be sure.
